pack.description: Vocabulary of geology passages and talks: rocks, plate movement, erosion and landforms.
pack.selection_note: Internal selection of terms that recur in introductory geology texts; this is not an official list and CEFR levels are author estimates.
pack.copyright_policy: Original content written for this app. No dictionary definition, ETS item or external word list was copied.

entries.definition: small pieces of rock, sand or mud that water or wind carries and then leaves somewhere
entries.example_academic: Layers of sediment at the bottom of the lake record thousands of years of climate history.
entries.example_spoken: The river looks brown because it's carrying so much sediment after the storm.

entries.definition: the slow wearing away of rock or soil by water, wind or ice
entries.example_academic: Coastal erosion has accelerated since the protective dunes were removed.
entries.example_spoken: They closed the cliff path because of erosion.

entries.definition: relating to the large moving pieces that form the outer layer of the Earth
entries.example_academic: Tectonic activity along the boundary explains the frequency of earthquakes in the region.
entries.example_spoken: Our professor showed an animation of tectonic plates drifting apart.

entries.definition: hot liquid rock found below the surface of the Earth
entries.example_academic: As magma rises toward the surface, dissolved gases begin to expand.
entries.example_spoken: Lava is just magma that has reached the surface, right?

entries.definition: the thick layer of hot rock between the outer shell of the Earth and its center
entries.example_academic: Slow currents in the mantle are thought to drive the movement of the plates.
entries.example_spoken: The diagram shows the mantle in orange, between the two other layers.

entries.definition: a long crack in the rock of the Earth where two sides can move past each other
entries.example_academic: Stress accumulates along the fault until the rock suddenly slips.
entries.example_spoken: The whole city is built right next to a major fault.

entries.definition: the hard outer layer of a planet
entries.example_academic: Oceanic crust is thinner but denser than the crust beneath the continents.
entries.example_spoken: We only studied the crust today; the deeper layers are next week.

entries.definition: connected with large masses of slowly moving ice, or with a period when ice covered much of the land
entries.example_academic: The valley owes its U-shaped profile to glacial erosion.
entries.example_spoken: That lake is glacial, which is why the water is so cold.

entries.definition: the gradual breaking down of rock where it stands, caused by rain, temperature changes or chemical action
entries.example_academic: Chemical weathering proceeds fastest in warm, humid climates.
entries.example_spoken: The statues have lost their faces through centuries of weathering.

entries.definition: a large low area of land, often where water or sediment collects
entries.example_academic: The basin gradually filled with sand washed down from the surrounding mountains.
entries.example_spoken: The whole river basin floods almost every spring.

entries.definition: relating to earthquakes or other shaking of the ground
entries.example_academic: Seismic waves travel at different speeds through solid and liquid layers.
entries.example_spoken: There was some seismic activity last night, but nobody felt it.

entries.definition: an occasion when a volcano suddenly throws out burning rock, ash and gas
entries.example_academic: The eruption released enough ash to lower global temperatures for two years.
entries.example_spoken: Flights were cancelled for a week after the eruption.

entries.definition: to become preserved in rock over a very long time, or to cause the remains of a living thing to do so
entries.example_academic: Soft tissue rarely fossilizes because it decays before minerals can replace it.
entries.example_spoken: They found fossilized footprints near the river.

entries.definition: to leave a layer of sand, mud or minerals in a place as water, ice or wind moves on
entries.example_academic: As the current slows, the river deposits its heaviest particles first.
entries.example_spoken: Every flood deposits a new layer of mud on the fields.

entries.definition: a large area of high, fairly flat land
entries.example_academic: The plateau was formed when the entire region was lifted without being folded.
entries.example_spoken: We drove for hours across a dry plateau.

entries.definition: the slow rising of part of the Earth's surface to a higher level
entries.example_academic: Continued uplift has exposed rocks that formed deep below the seabed.
entries.example_spoken: The guide said the cliffs are the result of uplift, not falling sea levels.

entries.definition: describing rock formed when hot liquid material from inside the Earth cools and becomes solid
entries.example_academic: Igneous rocks that cool slowly underground develop large, visible crystals.
entries.example_spoken: Granite is igneous, so we can rule out the first answer.

entries.definition: describing rock made from layers of sand, mud or shells pressed together over time
entries.example_academic: Most fossils are found in sedimentary rock, where burial was gentle and gradual.
entries.example_spoken: You can see the sedimentary layers really clearly in this photo.

entries.definition: describing rock whose structure has been changed by great heat or pressure
entries.example_academic: Marble is a metamorphic rock produced when limestone is subjected to intense heat.
entries.example_spoken: I always confuse metamorphic rocks with the ones that come from volcanoes.

entries.definition: one of several layers of rock or soil lying on top of each other
entries.example_academic: Each stratum corresponds to a distinct period of deposition.
entries.example_spoken: The oldest stratum is at the bottom, obviously.

entries.definition: the process in which one section of the Earth's outer shell slides beneath another
entries.example_academic: Subduction of the oceanic plate generates the deep earthquakes recorded offshore.
entries.example_spoken: That chain of volcanoes exists because of subduction.

entries.definition: the rigid outer part of the Earth, made of the surface layer and the top of the layer below it
entries.example_academic: The lithosphere is broken into plates that move a few centimeters per year.
entries.example_spoken: Is the lithosphere the same thing as the surface layer, or does it go deeper?

entries.definition: made of sand and soil that a river has left behind
entries.example_academic: Early farming communities settled on alluvial plains, where the soil was renewed each year.
entries.example_spoken: The vineyards are on alluvial soil down by the river.

entries.definition: a mass of rocks and earth carried and then left by a moving body of ice
entries.example_academic: A ridge of moraine marks the furthest advance of the ice sheet.
entries.example_spoken: That long hill is actually a moraine left by the ice.

entries.definition: a part of a rock formation that can be seen above the surface of the ground
entries.example_academic: Samples were collected from an outcrop on the northern slope.
entries.example_spoken: We stopped at an outcrop so everyone could look at the layers.

entries.definition: a long, narrow, deep opening in rock or in the ground
entries.example_academic: Steam escaped through a fissure that had opened on the side of the volcano.
entries.example_spoken: There's a huge fissure in the road after the earthquake.

entries.definition: very fine sand or mud carried by moving water and left at a river mouth or on a bed
entries.example_academic: Annual floods spread fertile silt across the valley floor.
entries.example_spoken: The harbor is filling up with silt again.

entries.definition: a small shaking movement of the ground
entries.example_academic: A series of minor tremors preceded the main earthquake by several days.
entries.example_spoken: Did you feel that tremor around midnight?

entries.definition: to form solid pieces with a regular shape as a liquid cools or dries
entries.example_academic: Minerals crystallize in a predictable order as the molten rock loses heat.
entries.example_spoken: If you leave the salt water out, it crystallizes on the edge of the glass.
